searchText: Sorry late to the party. May I ask how did the payload identify as orphaned in this case? I'm now downscoring peers that serve me orphaned payloads. But if you want to sync with those peers then you need to check with the beacon block if it's building on full or empty. The parent hash in the bid from block N is equal to the block hash in the bid of N-1? If yes it's full and the Payload of N-1 is included. If it's not then empty and the Payload is orphaned Correct me if I am wrong. Does it mean we can only know whether the Payload of N-1 is orphaned, after we've got the Block of N? yes, just like you can only know if the block for N is orphaned after you got the block for N+1 Right, so may I ask that how did the proposer of slot 4556 decide not to build on the Block and Payload at slot 4554? I assume it is by fork choice? yes, this is because of a bug in clients, that kept attestnig on the missing block 4555, the commitee for that slot voted for the blockroot of 4554 but with committee index = 0, that means *without* it's payload. Thus Prysm correctly goes to reorg that Payload. I believe Prysm is the only client that currently has this working in forkchoice that's why Prysm is struggling with a lot of reorgs Great thank you!

The parent hash in the bid from block N is equal to the block hash in the bid of N-1? If yes it's full and the Payload of N-1 is included. If it's not then empty and the Payload is orphaned

excerpts.content: Correct me if I am wrong. Does it mean we can only know whether the Payload of N-1 is orphaned, after we've got the Block of N?

excerpts.content: yes, just like you can only know if the block for  N is orphaned after you got the block for N+1

excerpts.author: 0xshum
excerpts.content: Right, so may I ask that how did the proposer of slot 4556 decide not to build on the Block and Payload at slot 4554?

excerpts.author: 0xshum
excerpts.content: I assume it is by fork choice?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yes, this is because of a bug in clients, that kept attestnig on the missing block 4555, the commitee for that slot voted for the blockroot of 4554 but with committee index = 0, that means *without* it's payload. Thus Prysm correctly goes to reorg that Payload. I believe Prysm is the only client that currently has this working in forkchoice that's why Prysm is struggling with a lot of reorgs
